key_insight: AI rewriting of radiology reports creates a “slop paradox”: cleaner-looking text can preserve or distort different kinds of information in opposite ways, with some rewrite styles strongly reducing clinical detail while leaving image-text alignment relatively intact.
clinical_relevance: For multimodal medical AI, the main risk is that documentation workflows meant to standardize reports may subtly weaken downstream training data quality, even when the text still appears clinically polished.
method: 450 chest X-ray reports from the Indiana University dataset
Three synthetic LLM rewriting tasks: EHR summarization, standardized rewriting, and teaching case preparation
Measured entity erosion, hedging loss, and BiomedCLIP image-text alignment change
evidence_signal: EHR summarization erased 51.4% of clinical entities and 43.7% of hedging language but only reduced image-text alignment by 2.5%, while the cleaner-looking rewriting tasks caused larger alignment drops of 14.9%–16.5%.
watch_item: Rare-pathology monitoring did not show a significant differential effect after correction, so content-specific safeguards alone may miss broader degradation caused by the rewriting style itself.
paper_title: The Slop Paradox: How Synthetic Standardization Erodes Clinical Uncertainty and Cross-Modal Alignment in AI-Rewritten Radiology Reports
